patterns.what_worked: Verifying the tree before editing paid off twice: git status was clean (so the 9-file diff is provably only this lane), and the TOCs are LF today despite the 2026-10-19 version-bump note saying CRLF - checking `grep -c $'\r'` instead of trusting the note meant the endings were preserved as found. Editing one unique line per file with an exact-match replace kept the diff to 10 paired lines, and running toc_check before AND after gave a stable 1104/0 baseline to compare against.
patterns.what_was_hard: The dispatch's line numbers only held for the live fields; the TOC version header sits at line 6 now while the prior desk journal records line 5, so the older note had to be treated as history rather than instruction. Also, git diff --stat cannot see the new desk files (untracked), so the scope proof needed git status --porcelain alongside it, not instead of it.
patterns.skill_gap: No automated pin guards version-field sync, so this lane's proof is one-off grep evidence rather than a durable regression test; that gap is filed rather than closed because tests/ is out of write scope.

escalation.recommendation: Reconcile the nine files and write the ## [2.1.7] CHANGELOG section once the parallel fix lanes land (deliberately not written here). Optional follow-up outside this lane: add a toc_check assertion that all seven TOCs plus main.lua carry an identical version string.
